existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `PaymentNotice` has a local hard break because R4 `provider` was replaced by R6 `reporter`. The main migration concerns are element rename/semantic drift, R6 notices that omit the formerly required `payment`, and R6-only `statusReason`; terminology confidence for `paymentStatus` is limited by missing local R6 CodeSystem/expansion evidence.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Forward R4-to-R6 migration is mostly straightforward except for `provider`: strict R6 parsers will reject the old element name, and implementers should decide whether each R4 provider really is the party reporting the notice. Backward R6-to-R4 conversion has greater data-loss risk because R6 can omit `payment` and can carry `statusReason`, neither of which maps cleanly into base R4 without either deriving data or using extensions.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local element/cardinality/type changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for terminology impact because the local ValueSets did not include expansions and the R6 core package did not include the `paymentstatus` CodeSystem resource even though the R6 ValueSet references that external system.
